summary: Describes how to use PPP over ISDN switched circuits. It is a standards-track proposal.

eli5.summary: PPP is a way to talk across a line. This explains how to do it over a dial-up digital phone line.

questions: how does ppp work on isdn circuits
how does ppp work over isdn
what framing does ppp use on isdn b channels
what is the ppp restart timer for isdn
subtitle: How to run PPP over ISDN channels, and which framing, encoding and timer choices make different vendors interoperate.

tldr.problem: PPP was built for point-to-point links, but ISDN offers many channels, several framings and several signal encodings, so two PPP implementations could easily fail to talk to each other.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC picks defaults for ISDN: full-duplex links, NRZ encoding on B-channels, bit-synchronous HDLC framing for first contact, and a few LCP and timer settings. It advises against relying on out-of-band call information.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard from May 1994 that gives implementers a common starting point, and the record lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

facts.label: Default network MTU limit
facts.value: 1500 (unless peer MRU of 2048 or greater negotiated)

facts.label: Encoding detection limit
facts.value: No more than 59 seconds (30 s preferred)

today: RFC 1618 is a Proposed Standard published in May 1994, and the record lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 1548 and RFC 1549.

sections.title: Why PPP Fits ISDN
sections.content:
RFC 1548 defines the Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) as a standard way to carry multi-protocol datagrams over point-to-point links. RFC 1618 describes its use over ISDN (Integrated Services Digital Network) switched circuits. An ISDN B-channel is by definition a point-to-point circuit, so PPP suits it well.

The ISDN Primary Rate Interface (PRI) can carry many B-channel links at once. PPP's LCP and NCP mechanisms reduce or remove hand configuration there and make it easier for different implementations to talk. The D-channel can also carry PPP packets if suitably framed, but it has limited bandwidth and often only reaches a local switch.

The RFC says PPP is not designed for multi-point or multi-access environments. It also admits there is unlikely ever to be one single worldwide ISDN, so it describes a few common implementations to promote interoperability.
sections.eli5: An ISDN channel is a private pipe between two ends, which is exactly what PPP expects. This RFC explains how to hook the two together.

sections.title: Physical Layer Requirements
sections.content:
PPP treats ISDN channels as bit or octet oriented synchronous links. The links MUST be full-duplex, but may be dedicated or circuit-switched. PPP gives the physical layer a stream of whole octets, with no provision for sub-octets, and the stream is applied mainly at the R or T reference points of the ISDN wiring model.

PPP places no limit on transmission rate beyond what the ISDN channel interface itself has. It does not require control signals, though using them when available can give more functionality and performance. Some framing techniques may need them, and that is outside this specification.
sections.eli5: The line has to let both sides talk at the same time, like a phone call rather than a walkie-talkie. PPP does not care how fast the line is.

sections.title: Bit Encoding and Automatic Detection
sections.content:
Encoding and scrambling are the job of the DTE/DCE equipment and are outside the scope. Still, the RFC recommends a default: the D-channel LAPD interface needs NRZ encoding at the T reference point, so NRZ is the recommended default on the B-channel there too. That lets frames move easily between B and D channels. Where encoding can be configured, NRZI is the recommended alternative to ensure a minimum density of ones on a clear B-channel. Inverted NRZ, used historically by some implementations, is deprecated.

Implementations that want to work with several encodings MAY detect them automatically, which matters most on Primary Rate Interfaces. The only reliable method is to switch between supported encodings. An LCP Configure-Request SHOULD be tried twice per mode before rotating to the next. Max-Configure MUST be set so the attempts total no more than 59 seconds before disconnect, though the usual limit of 30 seconds is preferred.

By prior configuration, other encodings may be used, but they are not recommended for auto-detection. The RFC deprecates V.120 terminal adapters, whose own rate-adaptation framing is hard to tell apart from Frame Relay and is not interoperable with bit-synchronous links. It also recommends the PPP Multi-Link Procedure instead of BONDING for using several B-channels in parallel.
sections.eli5: Two sides must agree how to write the ones and zeros on the wire. The RFC picks a favourite, and if a side is unsure it tries each way in turn, giving each a couple of tries, until the other end answers.

sections.title: Framing
sections.content:
On B-channels with no prior configuration, an implementation MUST first use bit-synchronous HDLC (from RFC 1549) for initial link establishment. This assumes that circuit-switched calls are generally host or router to host or router.

By prior configuration, octet-synchronous HDLC is recommended where the network termination equipment connects directly to the T reference point and octet boundaries are available. That equipment can drop bit-synchronous hardware, lowering part count and cost, and octet-synchronous HDLC MUST be used with NRZ bit encoding.

On D-channels, no data service is expected by default. By prior configuration, 'PPP in X.25' or 'PPP in Frame Relay' framing MAY be used. Multiple framing methods SHOULD NOT be used at once on the same ISDN channel, and PPP need not recognise or switch between framings without specific configuration.
sections.eli5: Framing is how you wrap each message so the receiver knows where one ends and the next begins. Start with the standard wrapping unless both sides were set up for another, and do not mix wrappings on one line.

sections.title: Out-of-Band Call Signaling
sections.content:
Experience showed that the LLC Information Element (LLC-IE) is not reliably carried end to end, because compatible switches are rare and provider policies vary. So its transmission SHOULD NOT be relied on to decide framing or encoding. No LLC-IE values for PPP have been assigned, and other values received are not valid for PPP links and can be ignored.

As an administrative alternative, several directory numbers can point to one physical access facility, each bound to a particular service. The called party identifier has proven to be reliably provided by the local switch.

When a called party identifier is used, or if a PPP value is ever assigned and received, a call MUST be rejected if LCP has not had the administrative Open event. Receivers MUST NOT accept an incoming call only to close the circuit or ignore its packets.
sections.eli5: The phone network's extra hints about a call are not trustworthy, so the RFC suggests giving each service its own phone number. And if you are not ready to answer, do not pick up and then hang up on the caller.

sections.title: Configuration Details
sections.content:
The LCP recommended sync configuration options and the standard LCP sync defaults apply to ISDN links. The network feeding the link typically has an MRU of either 1500, or 2048 or greater, so to avoid fragmentation the network-layer MTU SHOULD NOT exceed 1500 unless a peer MRU of 2048 or greater is specifically negotiated.

Instead of a constant Restart timer, exponential backoff is recommended: the Restart Timer SHOULD start at 250 milliseconds and end at 3 seconds. Implementations with persistent dialing, such as demand dialing or redialing, SHOULD limit their persistence, for example with exponential backoff or by discarding packet queues after a failed attempt to set up the link. Discarding the transmit queue can temporarily remove the stimulus to retry.
sections.eli5: Do not make packets bigger than the line's usual limit, and when a call fails, wait a bit longer each time before redialing instead of hammering the phone.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states only that security issues are not discussed in the memo. Any authentication or protection of the link is therefore left to PPP itself and to the deployment, not to this document.
sections.eli5: This RFC does not say anything about keeping the line safe from snoopers.
